result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [DataScan.to_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Export the profile as a JSON string. twitter-card: title: >- [DataScan.to_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Export the profile as a JSON string. title: >- [DataScan.to_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Export the profile as a JSON string. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Export the profile as a JSON string. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/datascan.py#L792-L837){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature DataScan.to_json() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} JSON is the format to use when a profile is stored outside of Python or sent to another system: in a database column, an object store, or an API response. The structure is the same as that of [`to_dict()`](`pointblank.DataScan.to_dict`), and [`from_json()`](`pointblank.DataScan.from_json`) restores a `DataScan` from it. Values that JSON can't represent directly, such as dates, are written as strings. To write the JSON to a file, use [`save_to_json()`](`pointblank.DataScan.save_to_json`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A JSON string representing the profile, indented by four spaces. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Here, a table of shipments with a date column is scanned and converted to JSON. ::: {#69354476 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl from datetime import date shipments = pl.DataFrame( {"shipped": [date(2025, 3, 1), date(2025, 3, 4), date(2025, 3, 9)]} ) profile_json = pb.DataScan(shipments, tbl_name="shipments").to_json() print(profile_json) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` { "metadata": { "table_name": "shipments", "row_count": 3, "columns": [ "shipped" ], "skipped_columns": {} }, "columns": [ { "colname": "shipped", "coltype": "Date", "sample_data": [ "2025-03-01", "2025-03-04", "2025-03-09" ], "statistics": { "n_missing": 0, "n_unique": 3, "min": "2025-03-01", "max": "2025-03-09" } } ] } ``` ::: ::: The earliest and latest dates are stored as strings. Because the result is text, it can be stored wherever text can, and [`from_json()`](`pointblank.DataScan.from_json`) turns it back into a `DataScan`.
